name: Southern Ma'di
catalog_citation: SIL International [Ma'di Urúléti translation team, Okollo Community Centre; no personal author named; PDF author field 'KY']. 2022. Léti Ma'di Urúléti làjʉ̀ wà kodrʉ vɨɨ / An Introduction to Reading Ma'di Urúléti. First edition. Entebbe/Uganda: SIL International. 4 pp. (one A4 sheet folded). SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 95008 ('A simple introduction to the Ma'di Urúléti orthography'; subjects: Writing System, Vowels, Tone Marks).
catalog_quote: 2. Tone. Maꞌdi Urúléti is spoken with tone. There are three main tone levels: high, mid, and low. The tone marks are placed above the vowels. High tone is marked with a line slanting up, low tone is marked with a line slanting down, while mid tone is unmarked. ... A few examples of why using tone marks is important for writing: orí 'snake', òrì 'fear', òrí 'lice'; tí 'cow', ti 'mouth', tì 'to flood'. ... 3. Long vowels ... Long vowels are written with the same letter twice. Each vowel is marked for tone.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Southern Ma'di (Ma'di Urúléti, Okollo) is a tone language with three level tones (high, mid, low), lexically contrastive (minimal triplets on monosyllables and disyllables); every vowel, including each half of a long vowel, bears its own tone. Nothing is said about word stress/accent.
new_statements.exceptions: none; contour tones not discussed in this leaflet (the unpublished Stolen 2020 phonology ms. has a 'Contour tones' section)
new_statements.identity_note: Ma'di Urúléti = 'Upper Ma'di' = Ma'di Okollo / Ma'di South, Madi-Okollo District, Uganda; SIL archives file it under Subject Language 'Southern Ma'di [snm]' and record 93283 calls Ma'di Uruleti 'a variety of the Southern Ma'di language [snm] spoken in Uganda'; contact address Okollo Community Centre. Not Moyo/Lokai Ma'di [mhi] and not standard Lugbara [lgg].

sources.note: Group-level survey statement: 'Even such intimately closely allied languages as MORU and MA'DI have quite different stress behaviour. In MORU stress is on the first syllable of disyllabic words.. In MA'DI, however, stress is on the final vowel: ˈléndrị, ˈléndr, iˈza, lɛ̀ˈdra. In both languages words within a phrase retain their original stress.' Nothing said about LUGBARA stress or about Okollo varieties. (Their MA'DI = Moyo/Sudan Ma'di [mhi].)
